casimir_effect.goal: Find the attractive Casimir force between two parallel plates of area A at separation a.

vars.a: plate separation (here in µm, so K is rescaled to 1.30e-3 N·µm⁴/m²)

casimir_effect.method: Only vacuum modes that fit between the plates survive; summing the missing zero-point energies gives a pressure that falls off as the fourth power of the gap, times the plate area.

precision_lithography.goal: Find the smallest feature size a lithography lens can print (Rayleigh criterion).

vars.NA: numerical aperture of the projection lens

precision_lithography.method: Diffraction blurs any image to roughly a wavelength divided by how wide a cone of light the lens collects; process tricks shrink it by the factor k1.

femtoengineering.goal: Find the photon energy needed to resolve (and engineer) a structure of size d, smaller than a proton.
femtoengineering.method: To see or shape a feature you need a probe whose wavelength is no bigger than it; a photon of wavelength λ carries energy hc/λ.

vacuum_energy_storage.goal: Find the energy released when a volume V of false vacuum relaxes to the true vacuum.

vars.ρ1: energy density of the false (higher) vacuum (J/m³)
vars.ρ2: energy density of the true (lower) vacuum (J/m³)

vacuum_energy_storage.method: Energy density times volume is energy; only the difference between the two vacuum levels can be extracted.

platonic_realm.goal: Find the number of edges of a Platonic solid from its vertices and faces (e.g. the dodecahedron).
platonic_realm.method: Euler's polyhedron formula V - E + F = 2 holds for every convex polyhedron; rearrange it for E.

topology.goal: Find the Hall conductance of a topological insulator state with Chern number ν (quantum Hall effect).

vars.ν: Chern number / filling factor (an integer topological invariant)

topology.method: The Hall conductance is a topological invariant: it can only change in integer steps, each step being one conductance quantum built from the charge squared over Planck's constant.

real_analysis.goal: Find the limit of the geometric series a + ar + ar² + ... (for |r| < 1).
real_analysis.method: Write the partial sum S_n, subtract r·S_n so all middle terms cancel, then let n go to infinity so r^n vanishes.

complex_analysis.goal: Find the modulus of each of the n complex n-th roots of a number with modulus r.

vars.r: modulus of the number being rooted
vars.n: order of the root (the polynomial degree)

complex_analysis.method: Write z = r·e^{iθ}; by de Moivre each of the n roots is r^(1/n)·e^{i(θ+2πk)/n}, so all share the same modulus and are spread evenly around a circle.

particle_physics.goal: Find the bending radius of a collider ring for protons of momentum p in dipole field B.
particle_physics.method: The Lorentz force qvB supplies the centripetal force, giving R = p/(qB); for unit charge, p in GeV/c and B in tesla the conversion factor is 0.3.

plasma_metallurgy.goal: Find the mean thermal kinetic energy of a particle in a stellar plasma at temperature T.
plasma_metallurgy.method: Equipartition gives kT/2 per quadratic degree of freedom, and a free particle has three translational degrees of freedom.

abstract_algebra.goal: Find how many imaginary units the algebra obtained after n Cayley-Dickson doublings of the reals has (complex, quaternions, octonions...).

vars.n: number of Cayley-Dickson doublings starting from the reals

abstract_algebra.method: Each doubling pairs two copies of the previous algebra, doubling the dimension; one basis element is the real unit, the rest are imaginary units.

dark_sector.goal: Find the mass enclosed within radius r of a galaxy with a flat rotation speed v - far more than the visible stars.

vars.G: gravitational constant in kpc·(km/s)²/(10¹⁰ solar masses), about 4.3e4

dark_sector.method: Set the gravitational acceleration GM/r² equal to the centripetal acceleration v²/r of a circular orbit and solve for M.

assembly_lines.goal: Find the total time a k-stage pipelined assembly line needs to produce N components.
assembly_lines.method: The first item takes k stage-times to fill the pipeline; after that one finished item drops out every stage-time.

set_theory.goal: Find how many elements the power set of the power set of an n-element set has.
set_theory.method: Each subset is a yes/no choice for every element, so a set with m elements has 2^m subsets; apply this twice.

quantum_field_theory.goal: Find the energy of a field excitation (particle) of mass m and wavenumber k, in units with ħ = c = 1.
quantum_field_theory.method: Plug a plane wave into the Klein-Gordon equation: each Fourier mode is a harmonic oscillator whose frequency obeys the relativistic energy-momentum relation.

general_intelligence.goal: Find the output of a sigmoid neuron - the building block of learning machines - with net input z.
general_intelligence.method: The logistic function squashes the weighted input into (0, 1); it equals one over one plus the exponential of the negated activation.

psionics.goal: Find the resting (Nernst) potential of a neuron for an ion species - the closest real 'crystallised thought' is the voltage of a nerve cell.

vars.Vt: thermal voltage kT/e (26.7 mV at body temperature)

psionics.method: At equilibrium the electrical work zeE balances the diffusion drive kT·ln of the concentration ratio across the membrane.

temporal_mechanics.goal: Find the entropy increase when n moles of gas expand freely from V1 to V2 - the thermodynamic arrow of time.
temporal_mechanics.method: Entropy is k·ln of the number of microstates; each molecule gains V2/V1 times as many positions, so ΔS is N·k·ln(V2/V1) = nR·ln(V2/V1).

stellar_evolution.goal: Find the main-sequence lifetime of a star of mass M (in solar masses).
stellar_evolution.method: Lifetime is fuel over burn rate: fuel scales with M and luminosity with roughly M^3.5, and the Sun lasts about 10 billion years.

holographic_principle.goal: Find the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy (in bits of kB) of a black hole of horizon radius r, which is a quarter of its area in Planck units.
holographic_principle.method: Black hole entropy is A/(4 lp²) - proportional to area, not volume; with A = 4πr² the factors of 4 cancel.

stellar_engineering.goal: Find the luminosity of the ignited captive star from its radius and surface temperature (Stefan-Boltzmann law in solar units).
stellar_engineering.method: A star radiates like a black body: σT⁴ per unit area times the surface 4πR²; divide by the same expression for the Sun.

exotic_chemistry.goal: Find the Bohr radius of muonic hydrogen - a muon (mass m) orbiting a proton (mass M) - using the reduced mass.
exotic_chemistry.method: The Bohr radius is inversely proportional to the reduced mass μ = mM/(m+M); measured in electron masses this gives a0/μ.

supersymmetry.goal: Find the relic density of the lightest supersymmetric particle (a WIMP) from its annihilation cross-section.

vars.s: thermally averaged annihilation cross-section ⟨σv⟩ (units of 1e-26 cm³/s)

supersymmetry.method: WIMPs freeze out when annihilation can no longer keep up with expansion; the more they annihilate the fewer survive, giving Ωh² ≈ 3e-27 cm³/s / ⟨σv⟩.

synthetic_biology.goal: Find how many synthetic cells a culture holds after time t if it starts from N0 cells that divide every td hours.
synthetic_biology.method: Every division doubles the population, and t/td divisions happen in time t, so the count is multiplied by two that many times.

superconductivity.goal: Find the BCS critical temperature of a hydride superconductor from its Debye temperature and electron-phonon coupling.

vars.Θ: Debye temperature (K) - high for light hydrogen lattices

superconductivity.method: In BCS theory the Cooper-pair binding is non-perturbative in the coupling: the phonon energy cutoff is suppressed by an exponential in minus one over the coupling.

field_engineering.goal: Find the gravitational field strength a projector must reproduce at distance r from a mass M.
field_engineering.method: The field is force per unit test mass; Newton's law gives an inverse-square fall-off (Gauss's law for a spherical source).

quantum_gravity.goal: Find the Planck mass, where a particle's Compton wavelength equals its own Schwarzschild radius and quantum gravity takes over.
quantum_gravity.method: Set ħ/(mc) equal to Gm/c² (up to factors of order one) and solve for m.

superintelligence.goal: Find the capability of a self-improving mind after n rounds, if each round improves it by a fraction r.
superintelligence.method: Each round multiplies the current capability by (1 + r), so the gains compound geometrically like interest.

multiverse.goal: Find how many Hubble volumes (pocket universes) eternal inflation creates from one after time t.

vars.H: Hubble rate of the inflating false vacuum

multiverse.method: During inflation the scale factor grows as e^{Ht}; volume goes as the cube of the scale factor.

quantum_foam.goal: Find how long a virtual particle-antiparticle pair can borrow existence from the vacuum.

vars.c: speed of light (1 in these units)

quantum_foam.method: The energy-time uncertainty relation ΔE·Δt ≥ ħ/2 allows borrowing ΔE = 2mc² (two rest masses) for a time ħ/(2ΔE).

cosmogenesis.goal: Find the tunnelling exponent B for false vacuum decay in the thin-wall approximation (decay rate ∝ e^-B).

vars.ε: energy density difference between false and true vacuum

cosmogenesis.method: Coleman's bounce: a bubble costs wall energy ~σR² and gains ~εR³; extremising the Euclidean action gives R = 3σ/ε and B = 27π²σ⁴/(2ε³).

simulation_hypothesis.goal: Find the maximum number of bits a simulated region of radius R and energy E can hold (Bekenstein bound) - e.g. a proton.

vars.ħc: reduced Planck constant times c (197.3 MeV·fm)

simulation_hypothesis.method: Lower an object into a black hole: the second law forbids it carrying more entropy than the horizon area it adds, giving S ≤ 2πkRE/(ħc); divide by ln 2 for bits.

conceptual_singularities.goal: Find the minimum number of bits needed to compress a message of N symbols drawn uniformly from an alphabet of k symbols (Shannon source coding).

vars.N: number of symbols in the message

conceptual_singularities.method: Each symbol carries log2(k) bits of entropy and no lossless code beats the entropy; change base with ln(k)/ln(2).

transfinite_hierarchy.goal: Find how many square (2-dimensional) faces an n-dimensional hypercube has (e.g. the tesseract).
transfinite_hierarchy.method: A square face is fixed by choosing which 2 of the n coordinates vary (n choose 2 ways) and fixing each of the remaining n-2 coordinates to 0 or 1.

panspermia.goal: Find how many spores in a meteorite survive an interplanetary journey of time t under cosmic radiation.

vars.D0: dose that reduces survivors by a factor e (Gy)

panspermia.method: Each unit of dose kills a fixed fraction of the survivors, so survival decays exponentially in the total absorbed dose R·t.

hyperdimensional_reality.goal: Find how many universes the cosmic tree holds if every universe buds b daughters, down to depth d.

vars.d: depth of the tree (generations below the root)

hyperdimensional_reality.method: Generation g holds b^g universes; sum the geometric series 1 + b + ... + b^d by multiplying by (b-1) and cancelling the middle terms.

beyond_the_omega.goal: Find the de Sitter horizon entropy - the absolute information ceiling of a universe with cosmological constant Λ, the closest real limit to 'past the possible' (natural units).
beyond_the_omega.method: The cosmological horizon has radius sqrt(3/Λ); like a black hole, its entropy is a quarter of its area in Planck units (A/4lp² with lp² = ħG/c³).
